title: Covered-Case Instrument Return
instruction: Three opaque cases stand side by side in one row. Use the left arm to grasp each lid's central handle, lift it and slide it horizontally to the left of that case, clear of the right wrist camera's view. The right arm holds the incoming module and uses its wrist camera to check each opened case. If occupied, move the right arm away and replace that lid before checking another case. Case inspection order is unrestricted. Place the module only in a visually confirmed empty case, move the right arm clear, and replace its lid. Keep stored modules undisturbed and leave all three lids seated on their matching cases.
context: At a shared measurement bench, three opaque lidded cases protect interchangeable instrument modules. A returner must open a case to verify a vacant slot before releasing a module; stacking it on a stored module would disturb protected inventory. Reclosing the lids restores the storage state.
setup: Fixed seed-42 station layout, SI metres; +X away from the robot mounts, +Y left, +Z up. Unmodified YAM table (top z=0.7475 m), two arms, one top RGB camera and both wrist RGB cameras; object_jitter=0. Three identical closed opaque cases stand in one row at x=0.27 m, with y_i=(0.11, 0.00, -0.11) m for i=0,1,2. Cases 0 and 1 each contain one identical stored_0/stored_1 module; case 2 is empty. The policy instruction and RGB observation do not give the occupancy flag. Each module is a matte ochre rigid-polymer surrogate cube, 0.040 m on each side, mass 0.080 kg. Stored module centres are (0.27,0.11,0.7755) and (0.27,0.00,0.7755) m. The incoming module starts at (0.25,-0.33,0.7735) m on one fixed matte rigid 0.075 x 0.075 x 0.006 m intake pad centred at (0.25,-0.33,0.7505) m. For each i, the fixed case shell is matte polypropylene-like rigid plastic: one closed 0.096 x 0.096 x 0.006 m bottom centred at (0.27,y_i,0.7525) m; two 0.007 x 0.090 x 0.055 m X-side walls centred at (0.27 +/- 0.0415,y_i,0.7800) m; and two 0.078 x 0.007 x 0.055 m Y-side walls centred at (0.27,y_i +/- 0.0415,0.7800) m. The central 0.050 x 0.050 m placement footprint is a scoring region on the real bottom, not an additional box. Each lid_i is a free removable 0.075 kg compound rigid body at (0.27,y_i,0.8095) m. Its matching dark-plastic panel is 0.106 x 0.106 x 0.004 m; an underside outer skirt has two X strips 0.002 x 0.099 x 0.008 m at local x=+/-0.0485 m and two Y strips 0.095 x 0.002 x 0.008 m at local y=+/-0.0485 m. An underside inner ring has two X strips 0.002 x 0.071 x 0.008 m at local x=+/-0.0345 m and two Y strips 0.067 x 0.002 x 0.008 m at local y=+/-0.0345 m; all ring-strip centres are local z=-0.004 m. These two rings form a groove around the case rim with 0.0025 m side clearance. Each lid has one central high-grip 0.070 x 0.022 x 0.024 m handle centred at local (0,0,0.014) m. Case and lid shell contact uses static/dynamic friction 0.35/0.25 and restitution 0; handle contact uses 1.2/1.0 and restitution 0. The modules use the station object contact material. No logos, labels or extra parking pads are present.
scoring: End score, not best-ever score. A violation observed at a 20 Hz control step latches score 0: the incoming module leaves the workspace, or the incoming module enters an initially occupied case by at least 10 mm in both horizontal directions and 3 mm below the cavity top (including stacking on the stored module); it also gives 0 if a stored module is wholly expelled beyond its own cradle plus 5 mm, a lid is discarded, a mechanism loses integrity, or a task solid penetrates another by more than 3 mm. Case-opening order is unrestricted; full success does not require opening a second case if the first checked case is empty. Otherwise 0.25 when any case is physically open for 0.20 s; 0.50 when any two distinct cases have each been physically open for 0.20 s; 0.75 when that empty case has been open for at least 0.20 s and the incoming 40 mm cube is fully placed and released there, with all eight corners inside the 50 mm interior to 1.5 mm, its bottom supported within 2 mm and its orientation within 10 degrees of an equivalent aligned pose. Full score 1.0 requires both stored modules still correctly supported, all three lids released and seated on their matching physical case rims, and the incoming placement stable for 1 s with no violation and success termination within 2,400 steps. Released means both gripper collision-hull bounds are at least 8 mm from the incoming module, and any gripper within 60 mm is open at least 45 mm; stable means module speed relative to cradle at most 15 mm/s and angular speed at most 0.1 rad/s. A timeout is capped at 0.75. Before these milestones, the score is 0. Right-wrist RGB and actions can be inspected in the saved trial; visual understanding is not scored separately. The scoring and geometry code defines the exact predicates.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz (120 s of simulation).
reset_notes: A reset restores all objects, arms and scorer state to the fixed layout. No consumables.
fidelity: Three 75 g removable rigid lids have central handles and underside grooves. The 80 g modules and shells use simplified cuboid collision geometry. Gravity, contact, friction and grasping run in PhysX with unmodified YAM arms and cameras. Dimensions and materials are representative; no real-hardware calibration, contact-force measurement or continuous-collision proof has been performed. Scoring observes the state at 20 Hz; a brief forbidden crossing between control steps may be missed.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 (official task-file run, seed 42, 2,400 steps, max_steps); yam_scripted demo: 1.0 (same task file, seed 42, 1,633 steps, success).
